transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-16
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 55 mins
- Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Head of ML, Edenware), Tom Reynolds (CTO), Amina Saleh (Data Platform)

Summary (auto): quick discovery around model selection, context length and deployment mode. Customer needs long context (>65k tokens) for multi-doc summarization, multi-lingual support, and tool-calling to hit databases/APIs.

Transcript:
00:00 Jenna Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Priya, Tom, good to see you. We're Jenna Park from Redwood and Marco our SE is here as well, Marco over to you for a quick intro?
00:14 Marco Ruiz: Yeah thanks Jenna. Hi Priya, hi Tom. Quick agenda — understand your use cases, constraints, what languages and context you need, then go through model options (open models and variants), and deployment tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
00:29 Priya Nair: Cool, yeah short intro — we're Edenware, analytics for maritime docs, we ingest long reports, logs. Primary needs: 1) summarize batches of doc sets up to 50-100k tokens, 2) Spanish and Arabic quality is important, 3) need tool-calling for DB lookups and retrieving structured fields, and 4) tight latency for interactive UI (we'd like sub-700ms for single-turn ideally).
00:50 Jenna Park: Got it. When you say 50-100k tokens, is that prefix+generation or window total?
00:56 Priya Nair: Prefix + generation — the source docs alone can be 60-80k and we then ask multi-step queries, so we need long context.
01:08 Marco Ruiz: Okay good. On Redwood side we support long-context models — we have verified model variants that do 32k, 64k, 128k depending on model family and quantization. For very long docs our recommended pattern is prefixing plus KV cache and chunking with retrieval. Note: sometimes the transcription of internal docs, sorry — the KV cache is K-V cache, but internal notes might show 'K V cash' in some docs, ha.
01:32 Tom Reynolds: How does that map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? If we go hosted, do you have 128k models available?
01:41 Marco Ruiz: Hosted gives you access to our catalog including some 128k-capable open models, but Dedicated gives more control — you can pin a specific model variant and get reserved GPU pools which helps with predictable latency for interactive UI. Private is for VPC or on-prem if you need strict network isolation or regulatory requirements.
01:56 Priya Nair: For security, we require SOC 2 and customer-managed keys (KMS). Is KMS supported on Hosted?
02:03 Jenna Park: Yes we support KMS integration for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be configured with bring-your-own-key in some enterprise plans — we'll surface exact details in the security pack. We are SOC 2 compliant — we'll send the attestation.
02:18 Amina Saleh: Also need audit logs retention for 1 year; can we get token-level tracing?
02:23 Marco Ruiz: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route token-level cost and latency breakdowns and tracing hooks. Retention is configurable for enterprise customers; we'll include retention options in the doc.
02:37 Priya Nair: Back to models — we prefer open models to avoid vendor lock and to control cost. What do you recommend for EN/ES/AR and tool-calling?
02:47 Marco Ruiz: For multilingual with tool-calling, we typically recommend newer open T5-style or LLaMA family variants that have been instruction-tuned and tested for tool-calling. For Spanish/Arabic you want a model with strong multilingual pretraining — e.g., Mistral variants, Llama 3-type families, and some community-tuned Mistral-multilingual forks. We ran evals showing Spanish drop between models — I'll share the spreadsheets. Also tool calling is supported via function-calling and structured output; there are sometimes quirks with argument schemas in some open variants.
03:18 Tom Reynolds: Are there any quantization impacts on tool-calling or function-calls?
03:22 Marco Ruiz: Good question. Generally, 4-bit quantization can slightly alter output probabilities but function-calling semantic fidelity is usually fine. For mission-critical structured outputs we recommend running evaluation cases on the quantized variant — we'll spin up bench nodes for that in the POC.
03:39 Priya Nair: Latency — you mentioned sub-700ms. Is that realistic for 64k context?
03:45 Marco Ruiz: Context length and latency trade off a lot. For 64k context typically throughput drops and per-token latency increases; sub-700ms is aggressive for large context. For interactive UI we recommend a hybrid: precompute embeddings and retrieval to reduce prefix size, and use 8- or 16k working windows for the actual call. If you need true single-call 64-128k windows, Dedicated with reserved GPUs gives the best chance to meet tighter SLOs.
04:15 Priya Nair: Okay, so maybe a Dedicated pilot to validate latency and cost. What about cost delta between hosted and dedicated?
04:22 Jenna Park: Hosted is pay-as-you-go — easier to trial. Dedicated has commit pricing — lower unit costs at scale but requires a reservation and monthly commit. We'll send a cost model showing per-token costs across typical batching and caching profiles.
04:36 Tom Reynolds: Multilingual evals — can you share performance numbers for Spanish/Arabic on recommended models?
04:41 Marco Ruiz: Yes — action item for me. We'll include accuracy, latency, and token cost for base/open/quantized variants. Expect Spanish to be within 3-5% of English for the top multilingual variants, Arabic can be wider depending on specialized pretraining.
04:59 Amina Saleah: Tool-calling: we need secure connections to our DB and the ability to sign requests. Can Redwood support outbound VPC peering or private connectors?
05:08 Jenna Park: For Private deployments we can do direct peering and on-prem has full network control. Dedicated can be configured with private peering depending on region and contract. Hosted supports secure outbound through customer-managed proxies, but we'll need to work out network flow.
05:27 Priya Nair: Ok timeline — we want a POC within 2-3 weeks, internal stake holders include product and security. Success criteria: latency <1s for common queries, F1 >= 0.8 on key extraction, and reproducible tool-calls.
05:40 Jenna Park: Sounds good. We'll aim for a 2-week POC. Marco will run benchmarks with your sample data; we'll provide the model matrix and pricing.
05:48 Tom Reynolds: Any blockers on our side? We need to anonymize docs but can share structure and a few redacted reports.
05:54 Priya Nair: We'll prepare and share an S3 bucket link.
05:57 Marco Ruiz: Quick note — when you do long-context summarization it's often cheaper to run retrieval + chunking then synthesize, because token cost for 100k windows can be high. We have a caching layer and prefix KV cache that helps save costs on repeated prefixes.
06:15 Priya Nair: KV cache, yeah earlier you said KV-cache. Not sure the transcripter had 'K V cash' in some notes — ignore that.
06:22 Jenna Park: (laughs) we'll clean that up. Any questions on compliance?
06:26 Tom Reynolds: Just data residency — some customers require EU-only. Do you have region controls?
06:31 Marco Ruiz: Yes region controls and private control plane for Private options. We'll include a matrix of region availability.
06:39 Jenna Park: Great. Let's recap next steps. Marco will send the model matrix and recommended configs for 64k+ contexts, I'll send pricing and security attestation, Priya you'll share sample dataset. We schedule POC for next week.
06:55 Priya Nair: Works for us. Thanks everyone.
07:00 Meeting ends.
